extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties involved in PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, counsel, experts)
extracted.subtask_description: Applying PTAB standards for obviousness and discretionary institution in an inter partes review: evaluating whether prior art teachings (individually or in combination) render claim limitations obvious, whether there was motivation and a reasonable expectation of success, and whether institution should be denied under General Plastic factors. Focus is on clinical-trial-style claim limitations and related evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness — combined teachings (In re Mouttet)
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is what the combined teachings of the references would have suggested to those having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate references both individually and collectively to determine whether a person of ordinary skill would have found the claimed limitation obvious. See In re Mouttet, 686 F.3d 1322, 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine references
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must demonstrate that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have been motivated to modify or combine the prior art references to arrive at the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the record supplies a persuasive reason (e.g., to reduce risks, improve safety, or address a known problem) that would have led a skilled artisan to adopt the prior teachings. KSR v. Teleflex guidance (550 U.S. 2007) is applied when asserting motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a reasonable expectation that combining or applying prior art teachings would succeed in achieving the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a POSA would have reasonably expected the modifications or combinations to work in the claimed context (e.g., applying exclusion criteria to a different anti-VEGF agent). Evidence such as expert testimony that the expected outcome is predictable supports this factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping ranges establish prima facie obviousness (In re Peterson / Genentech)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases involving overlapping ranges, even a slight overlap in range establishes a prima facie case of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claim temporal or numeric ranges overlap with prior art ranges (e.g., 2 weeks claimed vs. 30 days/4 weeks prior art), that overlap can be sufficient to show obviousness absent persuasive contrary evidence. See In re Peterson, 315 F.3d 1325 (Fed. Cir. 2003); Genentech, Inc. v. Hospira Inc., 946 F.3d 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of hindsight reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: An obviousness determination must not rely on knowledge gleaned only from the applicant's disclosure; reconstruction must use only knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the analysis does not impermissibly use the claimed invention as a template to piece together prior art. In re McLaughlin (443 F.2d 1392) summarizes that reconstructions are proper only when they do not include applicant-only knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of prior art to teach or suggest each claim limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art references must teach or suggest the specific claim limitation (either individually or in combination) to support an obviousness conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether the references, taken together, encompass the claimed subject matter (e.g., whether MACTEL and CATT’s exclusion criteria would include 'any ocular or periocular infection within the last 2 weeks prior to treatment'). If the combined teachings reasonably include the claimed limitation, that supports obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether substitution of one reference's disclosure would alter claimed population or result
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether substituting a prior art disclosure for a claimed limitation would result in treating a materially different group or producing different results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substitution causes a different patient population or outcome (e.g., MACTEL’s 30-day chronic history versus claimed 2-week prior infection), explain why that difference is or is not material to obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility and weight of expert testimony and standard-of-care evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony (e.g., on how terms like 'chronic'/'acute' are understood, and on standard medical practice) and evidence of standard-of-care practices inform obviousness and motivation analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit persuasive expert opinions that show how POSAs would interpret clinical terms and whether standard practice would have motivated particular exclusions (e.g., excluding active/recent infections before intravitreal injections). Consider documentary evidence (labels, prior study protocols) corroborating experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of inter-study vs intra-study protocol deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of deviations from a study's own protocol (intra-study deviations) does not establish that investigators would disregard other studies' exclusion criteria (inter-study variation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate investigator-level protocol noncompliance with a reason why skilled artisans would adopt different published exclusion criteria across studies; focus on the guiding objectives and standards of medical care across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for discretionary denial under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny institution of IPR under § 314(a) based on discretionary factors as articulated in General Plastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the multi-factor General Plastic analysis to determine whether institution should be denied, considering potential abuse via serial petitions and resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 1 — prior petitions by same petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same petitioner previously filed a petition directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated or serial challenges to the same claims by the same petitioner weigh toward discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 2 — petitioner knowledge of asserted prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether at the time of filing the first petition the petitioner knew of, or should have known of, the prior art asserted in the second petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner had prior knowledge of the art used in successive petitions, that militates in favor of discretionary denial unless adequately explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 3 — petitioner access to preliminary response/Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether at the time of filing the second petition the petitioner already received the patent owner’s preliminary response to the first petition or the Board’s decision on whether to institute review in the first petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a second petition after seeing the patent owner's response or the Board’s decision raises concern of strategic tailoring and can favor denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 4 — length of time between learning art and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The length of time that elapsed between the time the petitioner learned of the prior art asserted in the second petition and the filing of the second petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long unexplained delays in filing after learning of prior art can weigh toward denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 5 — adequacy of explanation for elapsed time
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner provides an adequate explanation for the time elapsed between multiple petitions directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persuasive justification for delay (e.g., new evidence, changed circumstances) can mitigate concerns that lead to discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 6 — finite resources of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the Board’s finite resources when evaluating multiple petitions against the same patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowing successive petitions would unduly strain Board resources or permit petitioners to 'have multiple bites,' this factor supports discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor 7 — §316(a)(11) one-year final determination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement under 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11) to issue a final determination not later than one year after institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical scheduling constraints imposed by the statutory one-year deadline may be considered when weighing whether institution of additional proceedings is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that obviousness arguments rely only on POSA knowledge (no applicant-only knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any obviousness reconstruction must take into account only knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time, not knowledge gleaned only from the patent specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure petitioner's case does not rely on teachings that would be known only from the patent under challenge; if it does, that suggests impermissible hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of whether prior art exclusion criteria reflect standard of care
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether exclusion criteria disclosed in prior art studies reflect routine safety precautions or the standard of care that a POSA would have adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art exclusion criteria are routine safety measures (e.g., excluding active ocular infection before intravitreal injection), that supports motivation to adopt them across agents and studies.
